tasks.prompt: Trace how changing a todo item to done can produce and dispatch a completion notification. Include the trigger condition, event storage, save interception, clearing, and declared notification handler. Does this prove a notification ran after a successful database commit? Cite precise checked-in source ranges and separate configuration from observed runtime behavior.

atoms.requirement: Done emits only on false-to-true transition and then assigns its backing field.
TodoItemCompletedEvent holds the item, derives from BaseEvent, whose INotification contract makes it a MediatR notification.
BaseEntity keeps domain events in a nonmapped read-only exposed collection and AddDomainEvent appends.
Update command handler sets Done and then awaits SaveChangesAsync.
SavingChanges and SavingChangesAsync dispatch before base saving callbacks; this is not evidence of post-successful-commit execution.
Dispatcher reads tracked BaseEntity events, materializes them, clears entity collections before awaiting Publish for each.
LogTodoItemCompleted declares INotificationHandler<TodoItemCompletedEvent> and logs its event type; application registers assembly scanning. This does not prove runtime activation.

tasks.prompt: Trace request validation failures through the application pipeline to the configured HTTP error response. What happens before the next handler is called, and what evidence connects the web exception handler? Cite precise checked-in source ranges and separate configuration from observed runtime behavior.

atoms.requirement: ValidationBehaviour receives IEnumerable<IValidator<TRequest>> and runs async validators with the cancellation token.
It aggregates errors, throws the application ValidationException when failures exist, and only otherwise invokes next.
ValidationException groups messages by property name into Errors.
ProblemDetailsExceptionHandler maps that exception to HTTP400 ValidationProblemDetails and writes the response.
Web DI registers the exception handler, startup invokes Web services and enables exception middleware; application registers validation behavior.

evidence.excerpt: builder.Services.AddExceptionHandler<ProblemDetailsExceptionHandler>();
app.UseExceptionHandler(options => { });
cfg.AddOpenBehavior(typeof(ValidationBehaviour<,>));

tasks.prompt: Review a proposed change to todo-list title uniqueness and length. Compare the create-command validator with the TodoList entity configuration: what needs coordination, and do those two files establish database-enforced uniqueness or protection against concurrent duplicate creation? Cite precise checked-in source ranges and separate configuration from observed runtime behavior.

atoms.requirement: Create validator enforces nonempty title and maximum200; entity configuration also requires title with maximum200, so changes must coordinate.

evidence.excerpt:
RuleFor(v => v.Title)
            .NotEmpty()
            .MaximumLength(200)
            .MustAsync(BeUniqueTitle)
                .WithMessage("'{PropertyName}' must be unique.")
                .WithErrorCode("Unique");

atoms.requirement: Uniqueness currently uses an async AnyAsync equality lookup through IApplicationDbContext, not a database constraint declaration.
Complete TodoListConfiguration defines title constraints and owned Colour, with no unique index configured in that class.
These two files do not establish database-enforced uniqueness or concurrent-creation protection; a lookup alone cannot guarantee it. Do not broaden absence to all migrations or a deployed database.
